itinerary.cal: A June-to-July objective while the Mowich face still holds snow and ice; both opened 2012 reports found the headwall icefall out of shape by August. Requires a Mount Rainier climbing permit and wilderness camp permit, and as a Mowich-to-White River traverse it usually takes 3-4 days with a car shuttle.
itinerary.totalNote: A 3-4 day traverse: up from Mowich Lake to a Ptarmigan Ridge camp, across the North Mowich Glacier to a high camp below the headwall, over Liberty Cap, and down the Emmons to Camp Schurman and White River.

days.title: Mowich Lake to Ptarmigan Ridge camp
days.objective: Reach the lower Ptarmigan Ridge bivy
days.note: Take the trail to Spray Park and follow the ridge toward Observation Rock. The 2012 parties camped at about 8,200 ft and 8,600 ft on Ptarmigan Ridge above the North Mowich Glacier.

days.title: Cross the North Mowich to high camp
days.objective: Move camp to about 10,000 ft below the headwall
days.note: Drop off the ridge on the snow fingers near 8,200 ft rather than lower down the scree; one party found descending to 8,500 ft on scree a mistake. Bivy sites around 9,200 ft are scarce, and one party camped just below the headwall near 10,000 ft, wearing helmets because of icefall.

days.title: Climb the headwall over Liberty Cap
days.objective: Top out on Liberty Cap and start down the Emmons
days.note: Leave before dawn. If the hourglass icefall is out of shape, the 2012 party used a snow ramp onto the central Mowich face instead, finishing on steep, sustained snow under a rock band. They needed an unplanned bivy between Liberty Cap and the summit, so carry bivy gear over the top.

days.title: Descend the Emmons to White River
days.objective: Return via Camp Schurman to the White River trailhead
days.note: Descend the Emmons-Winthrop route past Camp Schurman and out the Glacier Basin trail. One 2012 party descended Disappointment Cleaver to Paradise instead.

notes: Neither opened source climbs the North Mowich Headwall itself. Upwardescape (Aug 2012) found the headwall icefall out of shape, used a snow ramp onto the central face, camped at 8,600 ft and about 10,000 ft, bivied near Liberty Cap and descended the DC, not the Emmons. Turns-all-year (Jul 2012) camped at 8,200 ft on the North Mowich and climbed the central face. Day gains come from the row's 4,955 ft trailhead and 14,112 ft high point plus the source camp elevations. Row dist_km 27.36 (17.0 mi) fits a one-way Mowich-to-White River traverse; no source splits it by day, so day miles are left blank. The search found only a SummitPost Mowich Headwall page (403).

itinerary.cal: Usually climbed July through September once the Liberty Bell-Concord gully has melted out; earlier in the season carry an ice axe for the gully snow. No permit is needed beyond a recreation pass to park, and it is a single short day.
itinerary.totalNote: A short day trip: about 1.5 miles of Blue Lake trail and a climbers' path to the Liberty Bell-Concord notch, three short pitches on Concord Tower, and rappels back to the notch.

days.title: Concord Tower via the Cave Route variation
days.objective: Climb the variation to the summit and rappel to the notch
days.note: Leave the Blue Lake trail about 1.5 miles in and take the climbers' path up slabs and talus to the gully between Liberty Bell and Concord. From the notch, drop about 50 ft down the north side to the two diagonal cracks of the Cave Route. Climb its first pitch (the 5.8 crux), then go right at the roof into a 4-inch slabby crack and link the last two pitches. Rappel from the west side of the summit, with a final rappel down the first pitch of the North Face to the notch.

notes: Mountain Project's own page for this variation confirms it starts from the top of Cave Route P1 and links the last two pitches (listed 80 ft, Grade II); the Cave Route page gives the start, rappels and P1 crux. Steph Abegg gives just over an hour to climb the neighboring North Face and quick bolted rappels, but no car-to-car time, so hours are left blank. Gain runs from a trailhead near 5,200 ft (WTA: Blue Lake at 6,254 ft is 1,050 ft above it) to the row's 7,569 ft high point. CONTRADICTION: the row grades the route 5.6, but its first pitch is the Cave Route's 5.8 crux.

reason: No route description or trip report for a scramble on Three Musketeers Ridge. The session web-search budget ran out before the one planned search, and the row has no summit elevation, gain or distance.

No source describes the Northwest Ridge. The search found Dry Creek reports, SummitPost (403) noting that the north-side routes start from the Ice Caves viewpoint, and a 1974 AAJ note on a North Face gully (13 h round trip). None of these covers this route.
The Tower Route (on the NE ridge) appears only in passing in CascadeClimbers threads (403) and a SummitPost access note (403). No opened source gives its length, timing or descent.
The only description is a one-line SummitPost note ('ascend from Hester Lake trail; route finding and bushwhack'), seen as a search snippet; the page returns 403. No trip report covers this line.

The East Buttress is described only on SummitPost (Wing Lake start, gully system, class 3-4, 'long strenuous day or comfortable weekend'), seen as a search snippet; the page returns 403. No second source covers the route.
Only first-ascent history (June 1971) turned up. The Yellowleaf Burnt Boot page lists one 2012 trip that came from the Iceberg Lake side; none covers the north ridge or the Middle Fork ford.

itinerary.cal: A late-summer scramble once the Heineken gullies and the ridge are snow-free; earlier in the season expect steep snow that calls for an axe and crampons. Usually done as one long loop, with a bike stashed for the road back.
itinerary.totalNote: A single long day: about 20 miles and 8,700 ft of gain from Bedal Creek over Heineken Peak, up the NE ridge, and down through Glacier Basin and Monte Cristo, in just over 12 hours.

days.title: Bedal Creek over Heineken to Cadet
days.objective: Climb the NE ridge and loop out through Glacier Basin
days.note: Follow the brushy Bedal Creek trail into the basin under Sloan, climb about 1,000 ft to the ridge, and refill at Cadet Lake. The crux is the descent off Heineken, down steep, wet grass gullies to a 5,600 ft low point above the Mayflower Glacier. The NE ridge itself is class 3 at most on solid rock, with a scramble bypass and meltwater at the hanging glacier. Descend the steep, loose slope into Glacier Basin, walk out past Monte Cristo, and bike down from Barlow Pass.

notes: Only climberkyle (Sept 2023) describes this route: 20 mi including about 6 mi of downhill biking, 8,700 ft, just over 12 h car to car. WTA's Cadet Peak page covers only the Glacier Basin exit (16 mi RT, 5,000 ft, 7,186 ft summit, class 3), so this rests on one route source. A SummitPost snippet suggests a two-day version camping at Cadet Lake, but that page returns 403.

itinerary.cal: A summer scramble from mid-July into September once the north-side snow has gone; the Enchantment permit area limits overnight use, so parties do it as one long day. An Alpine Lakes Wilderness self-issue day permit is required.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: roughly 5,200 ft from the Stuart Lake trailhead, mostly cross-country through forest, brush and talus to the 8,638 ft summit.

days.title: Stuart Lake trail to Cannon summit
days.objective: Scramble the NW ridge to the summit and return
days.note: Leave the Stuart Lake trail before the Mountaineer Creek bridge (sources give 0.5-1.3 mi) and climb south through forest and brush to a flat area near 5,000 ft before heading up toward the ridge. The summit block is a steep friction slab. Early in the season the north slopes hold steep snow.

notes: Neither opened source climbs the NW ridge proper. Both use this approach as a one-day trip: hippohamster climbed the SW ridge (8.62 mi, 5,200 ft, about 13 h, summit about 6 h after a 5:30 am start), and Wenatchee Outdoors skied the NW face (summit ridge by 1:30 pm). Gain comes from the row's 3,404 ft trailhead to its 8,638 ft summit waypoint. Hours and miles are left blank because the only figures are for other lines. Search snippets of a 2016 Mountaineers report and a 2013 CascadeClimbers TR call the NW ridge a long, non-technical scramble, but both pages return 403. NOTE: the row's high_point_ft is null while its summit waypoint is labeled 'NE Ridge route point'.

itinerary.cal: Best from mid-July to early October when the high basin is reachable; water in the basin tarns becomes unreliable after mid-August. Glacier Peak Wilderness self-issue permit; most parties take 3 days and add Saska and Emerald from the same camp.
itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip: walk up the North Fork Entiat to a high meadow camp near 6,800 ft, climb Cardinal (often with Saska and Emerald) on day 2, and walk out on day 3.

days.title: North Fork Entiat to the high basin
days.objective: Camp in the basin between Emerald and Saska
days.note: About 8 miles of trail to Fox Camp, the last certain water, then about 1.5 miles more on the Pyramid trail to the basin. Climberkyle's party camped in a meadow near 6,800 ft below Cardinal after a long day with heavy packs.

days.title: Climb Cardinal from the northwest basin
days.objective: Reach the 8,590 ft summit and return to camp
days.note: Climb the snow in Cardinal's northwest basin to the summit ridge, then scramble the exposed ridge to the top, with some slab moves in boots. Parties linking Saska and Emerald first did not reach Cardinal until evening, so climb it first if it is the priority.

days.title: Walk out the North Fork Entiat
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach; climberkyle's party found the walk out somewhat faster.

notes: Neither source names the NW couloir or north ridge. Lemke climbed snow in Cardinal's NW basin to the summit ridge and then the exposed ridge (8,590 ft summit), approaching from Lake Chelan. Climberkyle took the Entiat side in 3 days with a 6,800 ft meadow camp, but did not name the Cardinal line. Day 1/3 miles (8 + 1.5) and the 3,880 ft trailhead come from the row's bivy notes. Day 2 gain runs from the 6,800 ft camp to the 8,590 ft summit, ignoring any intermediate dips.

reason: No source covering the Northwest Chimney on Cascade Peak could be found or opened. The session web-search budget ran out on the one search for it, and the previously found C-J col sources cover only Johannesburg routes.

itinerary.cal: Snow-free from about mid-July through September; earlier, steep snow on the north side calls for an axe and sometimes crampons. Overnight use needs an Enchantment permit, so most parties go car to car in one long day.
itinerary.totalNote: One long day of about 17 miles and 5,200-5,700 ft via Eightmile Lake, Lake Caroline and Windy Pass, finishing on class 3 north-side rock.

days.title: Eightmile trailhead to Cashmere summit
days.objective: Traverse the north side to the summit and return
days.note: Take the Eightmile Lake trail, turn off past Little Eightmile Lake toward Lake Caroline, and continue about 2 miles past the lake to Windy Pass. Follow the ridge northeast past the west-peak spires, cross to the north side, and traverse low below the summit pyramid to a class 3 gully or saddle that leads to the tiny summit. Wear helmets and keep the party close in the gullies.

notes: Both sources describe the standard north-side finish from Windy Pass (Outbound: traverse to a saddle just west of the summit, then a gully south; Wenatchee Outdoors: a class 3 gully that avoids 4th class), but neither calls it the northeast ridge, so the last few hundred feet may differ from the row's route. Figures: Outbound 17 mi RT / 5,700 ft; Wenatchee Outdoors 8.5-9 mi one way / 5,200-5,300 ft. Neither gives a time, so hours are blank.

reason: No new sources this run. The written-up approach crosses the border on foot from Manning Park, which is not lawful, and nothing found covers the lawful Harts Pass/PCT approach the row names (roughly 30 mi each way).
Only first-ascent material exists, and that party approached from Canada. Nothing found gives camps or timing for the lawful Ross Lake / Freezeout Creek approach to the north face.

The only route description is an OpenBeta entry seen as a search snippet (5.7, a long ridge 0.65 mi summit to summit, double ropes advised); the page 404'd on fetch. The other results were ski circumnavigations, so there is no sourced timing or day structure.

itinerary.cal: Climbed June through September; the Squire Creek ford and a tributary crossing are hard in early season or after storms. No permit is needed, and most parties take two days with a bivy at the grassy saddle at the start of the route.
itinerary.totalNote: Two days: about 2-3 hours to the grassy-saddle bivy, then 14 pitches (1,800 ft) of mostly bolted slab and ridge, rappels back down the route, and the hike out.

days.title: Squire Creek to the grassy saddle
days.objective: Reach the bivy at the base of the route
days.note: Walk the old road past the Trail #654 sign to two cut logs with old cable, take the boot track down and ford Squire Creek, then follow the climbers' track downstream and up through old growth and two gullies. The top of the second gully is steep and dirty and opens onto the grassy saddle, which has good bivy sites near the route.

days.title: Climb Concerto and rappel, hike out
days.objective: Climb 14 pitches to the summit crest and descend to the car
days.note: From the saddle, scramble down ramps for 20-30 m and cross the granite apron to a two-bolt anchor. The route has sustained 5.8 friction on pitches 2 and 7-10, and the last four pitches follow the Primal Scream ridge to a summit chain. Rappel the route on chain anchors; some rappels need a full 60 m rope. Carry a single rack to 3 inches.

notes: Mountain Project gives about 3 h to the saddle, the bivy, 14 pitches over 1,800 ft and a rappel descent. Climberkyle (2021) reached the same saddle exactly 2 h from the car, crossing Squire Creek on logs, and names Concerto as the cleaner line to the top of the wall. Day 1 gain runs from the row's 1,900 ft trailhead waypoint to the 3,249 ft saddle; day 2 gain is the route length. Miles are blank because no source gives the approach distance. CONTRADICTION: the row's gain_ft of 2,200 is well below trailhead-to-summit (1,900 to 4,958 ft, about 3,060 ft). Its trailhead elevation (1,900 ft) also differs from the Doorway Flake row's washout parking (1,170 ft) for the same approach.

reason: No source describes the East Face (the row's descent is 'presumed'). Northern Pickets approach material covers other routes, and CascadeClimbers/SummitPost return 403. No new searches were possible.

itinerary.cal: July through September; the east-facing slopes below the wall get sun most of the day and can slide while snow remains. No permit is needed, and parties climb it in a single day from the highway, sometimes from a bivy in the south basin.
itinerary.totalNote: One day: about 2 miles from the highway into the basin east of the peak, six pitches (two of them 5.10) on the East Face, then down the South Buttress or West Ridge.

days.title: Climb the East Face of Cutthroat
days.objective: Climb the face to the false summit and descend
days.note: From the pullout west of Washington Pass, take the cairned track down to cross State Creek and up into the basin south of the peak (about two hours with a pack). Round the base of the South Buttress into the east basin rather than taking the loose scree chimneys below the wall. Descend by the South Buttress (single 60 m rope) or the West Ridge if the buttress is busy.

notes: No opened source describes this 1976 Bard/Chouinard/Cunningham line pitch by pitch; the AAJ Swarm report only mentions it as 'farther right on the face'. A SummitPost snippet (page 403) gives III 5.10, 6 pitches, ending on the false summit. The approach and descent come from the AAJ (about 2 mi from the highway into the east basin) and Mountain Project (South Buttress and Swarm pages). Miles assume 2 mi each way. Gain runs from the row's 5,227 ft pullout to its 8,066 ft summit, and the two-hour basin figure is from the row's bivy notes. CONTRADICTION: the row's dist_km of 2 (1.2 mi) is shorter than AAJ's about 2 mi, and its gain_ft of 2,500 is below 5,227 to 8,066 ft.

itinerary.cal: A July-to-September route, first climbed in July 2023; the east-facing approach slopes can slide while snow remains. No permit is needed, and the first ascent was done in a single day from the highway.
itinerary.totalNote: One day: about 2 miles from the highway into the east basin, 8 pitches (850 ft, to 5.11c/d) on the East Face, then the summit and down the South Buttress.

days.title: Climb The Swarm on Cutthroat's east face
days.objective: Climb the 8 pitches, tag the summit and descend
days.note: Approach as for the North Ridge and round the base of the South Buttress into the east basin, avoiding the scree chimneys. Two easy pitches lead to a treed ledge, then four bolted-anchor headwall pitches of 5.10-5.11 (P3 finger crack is the highlight, P6 the crux), then easier ground to the South Buttress crest. Bring doubles to #3, a single #4 and offsets. Walk and downclimb (5.4) to the South Buttress humps, or take the West Ridge if others are on the buttress.

notes: Both Mountain Project and the AAJ first-ascent report (Willis/Perz, July 3, 2023) describe this route. The AAJ gives about 2 mi of approach from the highway into the east basin and a one-day ascent ending with the summit and a South Buttress descent; Mountain Project notes they descended that way because it was late. No source gives hours. Gain runs from the 5,227 ft pullout (East Face row waypoint) to the 8,066 ft summit, and miles assume 2 mi each way. The AAJ grades it 5.11c and Mountain Project's P6 is 5.11c/d, consistent with the row.

reason: The only opened source is the 1988 AAJ note (IV 5.10, about 4,000 ft, 'a difficult approach' to the northern cirque, topped out under a full moon). It gives no approach route, camps or descent. A second source (ademiller) 404'd and SummitPost returns 403.

itinerary.cal: June through September; the Squire Creek ford is hard in early season or after storms. No permit is needed, and most parties do it in a day from the road, though the grassy saddle offers a bivy.
itinerary.totalNote: One day: 2-3 hours to the grassy saddle, a 4th-class scramble to the far western wall, five pitches (about 700 ft, 5.9), and rappels back down the route.

days.title: Approach and climb Doorway Flake
days.objective: Climb five pitches and rappel to the base
days.note: Follow the South Face approach (ford Squire Creek, then two gullies) to the grassy saddle, continue west past the base of Skeena26, and scramble about 90 m of class 4 to the far western wall. The flake is about 6 m above the start. P2 has the 5.9 face moves past four bolts and a 'diving board' dihedral. Rappel the route on two 60 m ropes; bring a single rack to 4 inches.

notes: Mountain Project confirms 5 pitches, about 700 ft, Grade II 5.9, the 4th-class access from the Skeena26 base, a rappel descent and two 60 m ropes. Approach time is about 3 h per Mountain Project, but climberkyle (who climbed neighboring Skeena26 by the same approach) took exactly 2 h; no car-to-car time is given, so hours are blank. Gain is the row's 1,170 ft washout parking to the 3,249 ft saddle (2,079 ft) plus the 700 ft route, excluding the 4th-class scramble. Miles are blank because no source gives the approach distance.

itinerary.cal: A late-summer objective once the upper snow patch on the face has melted; it needs a North Cascades National Park wilderness permit for the Eldorado-area cross-country camps. Plan about 4 days, or 3 with a camp at Dorado Col or on the Marble Creek bench.
itinerary.totalNote: About 4 days: the Eldorado approach to a lower and then a high camp near the East Ridge, a long climb day over Dorado Col to the 8-pitch Southwest Face, and a walk out.

days.title: Eldorado trailhead to lower camp
days.objective: Reach the lower camp near 5,400 ft
days.note: The standard Eldorado climbers' route is steep and is the hardest day of the trip with an overnight pack.

days.title: Up to the East Ridge high camp
days.objective: Camp near 7,800 ft at the base of Eldorado's East Ridge
days.note: Climb along the southern edge of the Inspiration Glacier to the bivy at the base of the East Ridge. Dorado Col and a bench near 6,000 ft in the Marble Creek cirque are alternative camps closer to the climb.

days.title: Climb the Southwest Face
days.objective: Cross Dorado Col, climb 8 pitches and return to camp
days.note: Cross the Inspiration and McAllister glaciers to Dorado Col, descend bare ice and snow to about 6,000 ft, and contour west on a bench to a snow gully below the face. The route follows the main crack system (wet 5.9 roof crux) to the ridge crest, then several low-fifth pitches on poorer rock. The NPS party descended by a single-rope rappel west to the Marble Creek glacier, then a loose gully rappel and a moat, and retraced their route over Dorado Col.

days.title: Walk out to the Eldorado trailhead
days.objective: Descend from high camp to the car
days.note: Reverse the Eldorado approach from about 7,800 ft to the trailhead near 2,100 ft.

notes: NPS and Mountain Project both describe this route (8 pitches, 1,400 ft, 5.9, approach over Dorado Col and the Marble Creek cirque) and the NPS camps, but no opened source gives a time for any day. Day 1-2 gains and camp elevations (2,100 / 5,400 / 7,800 ft) come from North Cascades Mountain Guides' Eldorado itinerary. Day 3 gain counts only the 1,400 ft route; the re-climb from the 6,000 ft bench back over Dorado Col is not given by any source and is not counted. The row has no gain or distance to compare.
